name: Lichen
description: Symbiotic composite intelligence merging fungal and algal systems into a unified organism capable of extreme environment colonization and mineral weathering.

core_attributes.pattern: symbiotic fusion, mineral weathering, desiccation tolerance

scope.definition: Rock weathering rate enhancement by lichen compared to bare rock control — expressed as ratio of dissolution rate per unit area per year under equivalent climatic conditions.

evidence.source: Brady et al. (1999) 'Rates and mechanisms of biotite dissolution under conditions relevant to pedogenesis', Chemical Geology 158:141-164; Banfield & Nealson (1997) 'Geomicrobiology', Mineralogical Society of America.
cross_domain_examples: lichen-covered granite weathers 3-8× faster than bare granite surfaces in field comparison studies
organic acids (oxalic, gluconic) from lichen: dissolve silicate minerals at pH 3-4 — biochemical weathering
pioneer soil formation: lichen on bare rock creates first organic layer enabling subsequent plant colonization

scope.falsifiability: If lichen-covered rocks show statistically identical dissolution rates to bare rock controls under same conditions, lichen biochemical weathering is not significant compared to abiotic weathering.
scope.measurement_limits: Weathering rate is species-dependent — crustose lichen are more effective than foliose due to intimate rock contact. Measurement requires controlling for microclimate differences between lichen-covered and bare surfaces.
